channel.title: Our Favourite Places Yorkshire Events
channel.description: Upcoming Yorkshire events from Our Favourite Places.

item.title: Figures & Fabric: Wes Anderson Inspired Life Drawing
item.description: An evening of costumed life drawing presented by Figures and Fabric at Showroom in celebration of filmmaker Wes Anderson.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Turning at Bly Manor
item.description: Travelling the liminal space between the supernatural and the depths of the human psyche, The Turning at Bly Manor winds the essentials of psychological horror around one pervasive emotion – unease. Based on Henry James ghost stories.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: A Sound is Still a Sound
item.description: Open Works Festival presents a rehearsed reading of A Sound is Still a sound. A kaleidoscopic play that spans one boozy night out in Coventry as Tyrell tries to apologise to his ex for forgetting about her birthday.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Coral
item.description: The Coral's mix of music hall, West Coast psychedelia, merseybeat, folk, jangle pop, garage rock, dub, reggae and more set them apart from their landfill contemporaries of the mid-noughties. The group continue to explore, experiment and evolve.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Kalakuther: Queen of Fela's Republic
item.description: 18 February 1977. One thousand soldiers stormed the Kalakuta Republic. They burned the compound to the ground and murdered Nigeria's matriarch of activism, Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti. The Kalakuta Queens rebuilt the revolution from the ashes.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Black History Month 2026 – Winter Garden Celebrations
item.description: Over three days expect to be entertained, informed and delighted by a powerful mix of music, storytelling, tasty food and fashion, plus free face painting for the children. Family friendly, accessible and all communities welcomed.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Sinners
item.description: Showroom's Black History Month season kicks off with Sinners. Before and after the film, the cafe bar will be an open space for members of the community to meet – with poetry from Sarah Louise and music from Sheffield DJ collective Calabash.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Wonder Stuff and Inspiral Carpets
item.description: Join the Wonder Stuff as they celebrate their 40th anniversary, supported by their old friends, Inspiral Carpets.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Americana: Gershwin & Bernstein for Trumpet
item.description: Award-winning rising star trumpeter Matilda Lloyd joins Music in the Round's resident Ensemble 360 for a sparkling celebration of American music, alongside some dazzling trumpet classics.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Wild Traditions: Jess & Rich Arrowsmith
item.description: Sheffield legends Jess and Rich Arrowsmith launch their new album As Merry As May Be.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Seven Magic Birds: An African Panto
item.description: Open Works Festival presents a work in progress performance. What happens when the rules and conventions of a British pantomime are thrown into chaos by an African folktale? Let's find out together.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Black History Month: We Are the Storytellers
item.description: A youth-led film and arts programme working with five talented youth groups across Sheffield.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Tchotchke
item.description: Drawing on the sass and attitude of 60s girl groups, the theatrics of outsider pop acts like Sparks and Harry Nilsson and the canonical pop hooks of the Beach Boys, this New York trio present their own candy-coated take on rock’n’roll.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Britallica
item.description: The world’s first Britney Spears metal tribute. Bringing Britney’s biggest pop anthems into the world of heavy metal – and where better for it than Corp, Sheffield's home of all things rock and alt.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: In Conversation with Lolita Chakrabarti, David Greg and John Rwothomack
item.description: Join actor and playwright Lolita Chakrabarti, playwright and theatre director David Greig and Artistic director of Roots Mbili Theatre John Rwothomack in conversation.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The bEAT
item.description: The legendary 2-tone group come to Sheffield.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Thomas Carter & Geb
item.description: A spellbinding evening of contemporary folk in the atmospheric Samuel Worth Chapel.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Rory Green
item.description: Beautiful atmospheric music full of layered sounds and infectious rhythms. Ghanaian-English guitarist, composer and producer Rory Green joins Jazz at The Lescar following appearances at Lancaster Jazz Festival and Manchester Jazz Festival.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: ÌLỌ́YÁ... the Journey Begins
item.description: Mokan has it all figured out. Get the dream job at Shell. Build his father that house. Marry his sweetheart Sade. Simple. Except Lagos has other plans.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Martin Simpson Trio
item.description: Legendary guitarist and songwriter Martin Simpson comes to Sheffield with his Some Kind of Jubilee tour.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Paint Your Poetry Workshop
item.description: Join Poets Yield Power for a creative expression workshop, combining spoken word and visual art.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: No Bounds
item.description: A weekend of bleeps, beats and sweaty grins – exploring the relationship between music, art, technology and place. The 2026 lineup includes: Mark Fell, Blawan, Oppidan, The Black Dog and lots more.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Sheffield Comic Arts Fair
item.description: A showcase of indie and small press comic creators from Sheffield and further afield. With a Graphic Novel Reading Room corner, a kids workshop and bar.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Eddi Reader
item.description: Celebrating over 40 years as a live performer, Eddi Reader has effortlessly developed into one of popular music’s most thrilling and affecting performers.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Ijakadi (The Wrestle)
item.description: An intimate and thought-provoking performance exploring what it means to grow up carrying other people’s ideas about your worth. Blending spoken word, movement, live African percussion and visual storytelling.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Jazzing for Jamaica
item.description: A celebration of Jamaican culture, music, and community spirit, raising funds for the Jamaican Hurricane Appeal. Headlining the evening will be the internationally acclaimed Michael "Bammi" Rose Quartet.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: I Love Boosters
item.description: A group of shoplifters take aim at a cutthroat fashion maven by stealing her clothes and reselling them at a lower price, what they call "fashion-forward philanthropy."
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The New Eden: JC Niala
item.description: An urgent new voice in nature writing JC Niala explores wildlife in our cities, reframing our perception of co-existing with the natural world. Part of Off the Shelf Festival of Words.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Black-Owned Markets
item.description: Cutlery Works showcases black-owned businesses with over 12 stall holders offering a range of products, from beauty, fashion to baked goods. With live music and entertainment.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Orchestra Baobab
item.description: An institution of African music, led by Nick Gold of Buena Vista Social Club. More than 50 years on from their formation, the group’s mix of Afro-Cuban rhythms, Wolof griot traditions, mbalax, Congolese rumba and jazz, sounds as fresh as ever.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
item.description: A hilarious spoof of a classic tale from Sheffield's amateur theatre company Tudor Players.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: 6+1: All We Gain from What We Lost
item.description: Follow the story of the 6+1 Running Club, from its early days of low numbers and self-doubt through to the moment running became a form of therapy for its members. Plus Q&A with Director Lando Vandross and members of 6+1.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Goal of Our Health
item.description: A new solo exhibition at Site Gallery by New York and Glasgow-based artist and filmmaker Alexis Kyle Mitchell.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Vaughan Williams: Songs of Travel
item.description: Music in the Round’s Singer-in-Residence Roderick Williams returns with a programme of heartrendingly beautiful English song, including Vaughan Williams’ glorious cycle Songs of Travel.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Tangram: Rituals for a Changing World
item.description: From the intimate to the divine: an intriguing musical exploration of Chinese music and philosophy alongside European classical traditions in the Crucible Playhouse with Music in the Round.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Water Bodies: Memories, Landscapes, Mythologies
item.description: Join artist Eelyn Lee for a free sound, movement, and costume workshop exploring how Sheffield’s rivers carry memories across places and time. Starting with a short walk to where the river Sheaf meets the Don.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: When We Ruled: The Rise and Fall of Twelve African Queens and Warriors
item.description: Discover the fascinating history of queens and warriors who ruled vast swathes of the African continent from pre-colonial Nigeria to the villages of Rwanda, the hills of Madagascar to apartheid South Africa. With historian Paula Akpan.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Richard Ayoade: Afterthoughts
item.description: Join BAFTA-winning actor, comedian, director, and writer Richard Ayoade for an evening of reflections as he shares insights from his latest book, Afterthoughts, or Some Pistachios Won't Open: Wisdom for the Unreflective.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Charlie Chaplin: The Gold Rush
item.description: Charlie Chaplin’s most ambitious and successful silent comedy presented in a gorgeous restoration. With Chaplin’s own Academy Award-nominated score, performed live by Music in the Round residents, Ensemble 360 and friends, conducted by George Morton.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Kiell Smith-Bynoe & Friends: Kool Story Bro
item.description: Kiell Smith-Bynoe (Ghosts, Taskmaster, Stath Lets Flats) brings his smash hit improv comedy show to Sheffield.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Lady Leshurr – 10 Years of The Queen's Speech
item.description: The rapper and producer heads out on tour this autumn to celebrate the 10th anniversary of The Queen’s Speech series with a special run of intimate headline shows.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Steel City Beer & Cider Festival
item.description: Sheffield CAMRA (Campaign for Real Ale) know a thing or two about good beer, cider and perry. Join them for their 50th edition in 2026.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Mark Thomas: 40 In Stand Up Years
item.description: One of our oldest surviving alternative comics celebrates 40 years at the mic as he brings his brand-new show to Sheffield.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Site Gallery Creative Producers: Stories We Carry
item.description: Curated by Site Gallery’s Creative Producers, Stories We Carry is a short film programme about different black stories across the UK. Followed by a Q&A with the Creative Producers.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Sensoria
item.description: Sheffield's festival of film and music. With a robotic botanical installation in the old John Lewis. A performance inspired by cult 70s album Plantasia. A night of vinyl film scores mixed with VHS cinema. And more.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Celluloid Screams
item.description: Sheffield’s horror film festival returns every October – getting you spooked just in time for Halloween.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Tekkonkinkreet (2006) 20th Anniversary screening
item.description: Sensoria Festival in association with Reel Steel, present the rarely-screened cult anime classic Tekkonkinkreet (2006) in a 20th Anniversary 4k restoration.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: What We Leave We Carry: Voices of Migration to Britain – Colin Grant
item.description: What do we leave behind when we move to a new place – and what do we carry with us, physically and emotionally, wherever we land? Here are the voices of many people who have come to Britain to make a new life.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Crush
item.description: A clinic waiting room. Two Somali teens. One awkward meet-cute. Crush is a tender, funny and honest story about identity, connection and the messy path to healing.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Beethoven & Brahms String Quartets
item.description: Opus 13, the most recent winner of the prestigious Wigmore Hall International String Quartet competition, makes its Sheffield debut with a programme of bold and lyrical works.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Soul II Soul
item.description: The iconic band born from the vibrant UK sound system culture. Emerging in the multicultural melting pot of London, Soul II Soul transformed ordinary house parties into extraordinary experiences with their innovative and immersive performances.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Black History Month Community Civic Service
item.description: Sheffield Cathedral host the third annual Community Civic Service for Black History Month. With inspiring local speakers from the city’s Black-led churches, powerful gospel music, and information stands from community organisations.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Cabaret Voltaire
item.description: The iconic Sheffield band return to the Octagon, for the final date of their final tour.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Trauma Or, Monsters All [+ Larry Fessenden Q&A]
item.description: A writer investigating her town's dark past for a newspaper article stirs up fears about lurking monsters in director Larry Fessenden’s concluding chapter of his monster quadrilogy. Followed by an extended Q&A.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Waking the Warriors: Ben Okri
item.description: Acclaimed novelist, essayist, playwright and poet talks about his latest work, Waking the Warriors, a modern fable, born from the ancient legend of the sleeping warriors who wake when the kingdom is in mortal danger.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: We Were Here: Stephanie Phillips
item.description: A reclamation of alternative music history, for the Black artists who helped pioneer and shape it. Stephanie Phillips is a music journalist and musician who started Black feminist punk band Big Joanie and is part of the Decolonise Fest collective.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Greentop’s October Half Term Holiday Circus Clubs
item.description: Discover a world of aerials, acrobatics, juggling, creativity and performance at Greentop’s holiday circus clubs.
item.location: Greentop Community Circus Centre, St Thomas Building, 74 Holywell Road, S4 8AS
item.ify:location: Greentop Community Circus Centre, St Thomas Building, 74 Holywell Road, S4 8AS
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Witching Tale, Jan Doyle Band & The Greystone Sisters
item.description: A mysterious, spellbinding Halloween show at the Samuel Worth Chapel, featuring The Witching Tale.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: WTF: Audition [4K Restoration]
item.description: This disturbing Japanese thriller follows Aoyama (Ryo Ishibashi), a widower who decides to start dating again. Aided by a film-producer friend (Miyuki Matsuda), Aoyama uses auditions for a fake production to function as a dating service.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Tim Burton’s Universe by Mystery Ensemble
item.description: What better way to celebrate Halloween than an evening of the weird, wonderful and slightly macabre sounds of Tim Burton’s longtime collaborator Danny Elfman. With music from The Nightmare Before Christmas, Edward Scissorhands, Beetlejuice and more.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Sheffield Print Fair
item.description: Enjoy watching printmaking in action and pick up a print or two to take home from among the 43 stalls featuring the wares of artists and printmakers from Sheffield and beyond. Call for applications open till 30 August 2026.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Scooby-Doo Double Bill
item.description: This Halloween, join the Showroom on Spooky Island and in Coolsville for the ultimate double-bill, Scooby-Doo and Scooby-Doo 2: Monsters Unleashed.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Void: A Horror Story
item.description: Dare you enter a world infected by fear? The Void is a sci-fi horror created for the stage, presented by Yorkshire company Thunder Road.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Mariam sings Amadou & Mariam
item.description: Hear Mariam’s vibrant, Malian, worldbeat music on the Octagon stage.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Sharrow Young Leaders presents... Good Burger
item.description: Showroom's BHM season closes with a celebration of young Black creativity and community. Good Burger (1997) is a comedy about two goofy high-school friends who take summer jobs at a local burger joint and try save it from being taken over by a chain.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Festival of the Mind
item.description: A biennial festival of new ideas. Bringing together the city's creative community and its academic minds through exhibitions, talks, screenings, performances and more.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Amy Matthews
item.description: Amy doesn’t get angry and she’s starting to feel left out, so she’s on a quest to feel fury. From what she can discern from the world around her, it appears to be all the rage… literally.
item.location: Foundry, Sheffield Student's Union, Western Bank, S10 2TG
item.ify:location: Foundry, Sheffield Student's Union, Western Bank, S10 2TG
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Elgar Piano Quintet
item.description: Pianist Martin Roscoe joins forces with the Brodskys, a quartet who have been performing for over 50 years to prizes and plaudits around the world.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Sounds of Now: Saxophone & Electronics
item.description: Praised for his “urgently visceral” playing (Tempo), London-based Canadian saxophonist David Zucchi is joined by Robert Laidlow for a programme of innovative works for saxophone and live electronics.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Wild Traditions: Rachel Newton
item.description: Join the award winning singer, harpist and composer in concert at Wild Traditions.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Spotlight: Platoon [40th Anniversary]
item.description: Writer/director Oliver Stone's personal and searing testament to the men who fought the war in Vietnam.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Chopin Nocturnes
item.description: "Poet of the piano” Pavel Kolesnikov is one of the world’s most exciting young pianists. Lauded for his amazing ability to cast new light on familiar repertoire, he makes his Music in the Round debut with a tour through Chopin's complete Nocturnes.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: WTF: Pink Floyd - The Wall
item.description: A confined but troubled rock star descends into madness as he physically and socially isolates himself from everyone. Screening as part of WTF, Showroom's monthly screening strand celebrating the films that make you say "What The F...ilm"!?
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: A Journey Through Nordic Music
item.description: Join a panel of musicians and experts who will shine a light on some of the composers and music featuring across Northern Lights, Music in the Round's weekend of elemental music from the frozen north.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Music from Iceland
item.description: A dazzling portrait of contemporary Icelandic music ranging from celebrated glacial works by Anna Thorvaldsdóttir and Oscar-winning Hildur Guðnadóttir, to new arrangements of Björk and Ólafur Arnalds’ haunting music for Broadchurch.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Bob Dylan
item.description: Widely acknowledged as one of the most important figures of the modern day and one of the greatest and most influential songwriters of all time, Bob Dylan has reshaped popular music by elevating lyric writing to a profound literary art form.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Sibelius & Grieg
item.description: Music in the Round's resident Ensemble 360 performs masterpieces and miniatures for strings and piano by two giants of Nordic classicism.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Engegård Quartet
item.description: Norway’s multi-award-winning Engegård Quartet brings its customary boldness, energy and freshness to Sheffield in a concert of Mozart, Beethoven and Grieg.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: ShAFF Retrospective Features – The Best Of 20 Years
item.description: Sheffield Adventure Film Festival first landed at the Showroom in March 2006. To mark this 20th anniversary, the team have crafted a weekend retrospective of some of the festival's very best features and shorts.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Northern Lights: Norwegian Folk
item.description: Formed under the midnight sun in the Lofoten Islands, Norway’s leading string quartet brings the rugged soul of the country to the stage, with arrangements of traditional joiks, haunting psalms and spirited bridal marches.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: The Snowman + Live Score
item.description: Unite the Union Brass Band present a special festive performance of the Christmas classic with a live score.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Beethoven Appassionata
item.description: Tim Horton performs an afternoon concert for Music in the Round, launching his a journey through Beethoven’s staggering achievements for piano, with works including his celebrated Appassionata sonata.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Reich: Electric Counterpoint
item.description: Scottish guitarist Sean Shibe presents a tour of four centuries of music, including Bach’s first cello suite, Steve Reich’s masterpiece Electric Counterpoint and a recent commission by the UK’s leading contemporary composer Thomas Adès.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.title: Wild Traditions: Arbrevyn
item.description: Arbrevyn perform a Christmas special concert. Featuring Cornish carols alongside more local carols and some of their favourite repertoire.
item.dc:creator: Our Favourite Places

item.description: A loose adaptation of the 14th-century poem Sir Gawain and the Green Knight, notable for its striking imagery and performances. Screening as part of the Showroom's monthly screening strand celebrating films that make you say "What The F...ilm"!?

item.title: Spotlight: Rocky [50th Anniversary - 4K Restoration]
item.description: Rocky Balboa is a Philadelphia club fighter who seems to be going nowhere. Part of Spotlight, the Showroom's monthly screenings of unforgettable films brought back to the big screen, chosen by staff.
